notes: Complete fix matching the reference at all sites, with notably good tests (heredoc brace, nested handle, snippet import, quoted '}' not closing a block); the strings.Join-based comparisons are slightly awkward.

Complete Token-method conversion matching the reference's coverage (minus the HasSuffix/"{}" niceties), with the strongest tests: heredoc brace, nested block, snippet import, and a quoted "}" that must not close a block.

Complete, consistent conversion of all brace checks via Token methods, with strong dispenser and parse tests plus an end-to-end adapt test that includes respond with a quoted '{' followed by a real block.
Same complete fix with thorough dispenser and parser tests, plus an end-to-end adapt test that is useful but extends beyond the caddyfile package.

Clean Token-method approach with very thorough unit, parse and integration adapt tests, but it misses the doImport `currentMappingKey == "{"` anonymous-block check, so a quoted '{' key there is still misclassified.

Clean Token-method approach but misses the doImport anonymous-block mapping-key check (line ~384), so a quoted "{" key there is still rejected; it adds good table tests plus an integration adapt test outside the package.

Consistently replaces every structural brace check in the dispenser and parser with unquoted-aware helpers, matching the reference; it misses only the quoted-address suffix check and the doc-comment updates, and its dispenser and parse tests cover args, blocks and an unclosed-block error.

Uses package-level isBlockOpen/isBlockClose helpers, nearly identical to the reference, covering the import-args anonymous-block check too; tests include nested blocks and an unclosed-block error case.

Idiomatic Token methods are applied at every brace check site, including the doImport anonymous-block check; tests cover quoted args, nested blocks, backticks and an error case, but it skips the quoted-address suffix tweak.
Same solid Token-method fix as C4, with a focused dispenser test and parse table cases including an unclosed-block error.
Correct and complete coverage of the brace checks; it adds slightly redundant Dispenser wrapper methods on top of the Token methods, and its parse tests check segments including a snippet import.

Covers every structural brace check the reference touches except the quoted-address HasSuffix case and the quoted "{}" branch; the extra private Dispenser wrapper methods add needless indirection, and the parser tests (including a snippet import) are good.

Clean recursive computation of the section dir with slugs, correctly preserving intermediate directories; Dir is set only when needed, and the test explicitly covers a slugged section under a non-section dir plus taxonomy and term.

The compact recursive sectionSlugDir correctly keeps intermediate directories and respects unnormalized paths; Dir is set only when a slug exists, and the test covers a nested slug under a non-section directory.

Replaces path segments by index (slash count of each slugged ancestor's base), so nested slugs and intermediate non-section directories come out correct; the override is applied cleanly via sectionBase/containerDir helpers, and the thorough test covers resources, deep nesting, taxonomy and term.

Segment-index replacement is robust to normalized versus unnormalized paths, the container-dir rewrite checks path boundaries, and the test is thorough, covering bundle resources, a nested slug under a non-section directory, and taxonomy and term pages.

Builds the slugged section dir from relative segments, sets Dir only when a slug exists, and handles intermediate dirs and unnormalized paths; the test covers an auto-created term under a slugged taxonomy but not nested slugged sections.

The iterative ancestor walk builds the slugged directory correctly, preserves intermediate directories and handles unnormalized paths; the tests cover the issue example, taxonomy and term pages but no nested slugged section.

When a section has a slug it returns parentDir + "/" + slug, dropping intermediate non-section directories (help/a/b with slug becomes /help/bes instead of /help/a/bes); it also relies on *pageState type assertions, and its tests miss this case.

When a section has a slug it returns parentDir+"/"+slug, which drops intermediate non-section directories (e.g. /help/a/b with a slug becomes /help/bes), and it relies on *pageState type assertions; the tests do not exercise a nested slug.

Recursive raw/slugged base computation with consistent unnormalized handling and a careful replacePathPrefix helper; it correctly propagates ancestor slugs to sections and leaves, and its test covers nested slugs, a deep leaf, taxonomy and term.

The recursive raw/slugged section-base computation is correct and handles intermediate non-section directories and DisablePathToLower; the prefix-replacement helper in page_paths.go is clean, though keeping both Section and SectionBaseWithSlugs is a little redundant.

Always computes Dir by splicing slugs innermost-first, which works for nesting and intermediate dirs; it relies on length arithmetic with normalized bases against possibly-unnormalized dirs and does not verify the prefix, which is somewhat fragile.

The concise inner-to-outer in-place segment replacement works, but it indexes a possibly unnormalized dir using normalized PathInfo().Base() lengths and never verifies the prefix, which is fragile under DisablePathToLower.

The most focused patch, with no unrelated edits; tests fit well into the existing consolidation table and include unit tests, but the logic lives in a public `lib/executor` function with a CLI-flag error message, and env or script shortcuts that wipe scenarios are not handled.

Clean post-consolidation rewrite that keeps exec/env/tags/options, rejects multiple scenarios and CLI shortcut flags, and extends the consolidation test table; it does not handle lower-layer scenarios being erased by higher-layer shortcuts (e.g. K6_ITERATIONS env), does not reject execution-segment flags, and adds an exported lib/executor API.

Detects conflicts neatly via the CLI config layer rather than flag lookups, and has good run-level tests using the logger hook; it does not test archive or cloud, does not handle lower-layer shortcuts, and adds unrelated proxy TestMain changes.

Works, but detects conflicts indirectly through cliConfig values, ignores the GetBool error, misses the cross-layer shortcut and execution-segment cases, and duplicates proxy-unset hacks across two TestMains.

Registers a dedicated flagset on run, archive and cloud run and rejects K6_* shortcut env vars, which guards the env-wipes-scenarios case though it is overly strict; tests include an archive round-trip, but there is a hand-rolled `countSubstr` and unrelated proxy changes.

Well-organized once.go that rejects both CLI flags and env-var shortcuts, avoiding silent scenario loss from env shortcuts (stricter than the 'discard' spec), with good integration and archive round-trip tests; the proxy-env test hack is unrelated noise and countSubstr just reimplements strings.Count.

A straightforward and correct post-consolidation rewrite with solid unit and run-level tests (including derive/validate); it lacks archive and cloud coverage, ignores lower-layer shortcut wiping, and adds unrelated proxy test-harness changes.

Straightforward, readable applyOnceMode with solid unit and run tests that also validate derivation; it shares the common gaps (lower-layer shortcuts erasing scenarios, execution segments) and adds an unrelated proxy-env change to the shared tests.Main.

Clean `applyOnce` placed after consolidation with good unit, archive-metadata, run and cloud-run (including local-execution) tests; but it pulls `tests.Main` (goleak plus blocking transport) into `internal/cmd`, adds unrelated proxy env changes, and misses lower-layer shortcuts and execution-segment conflicts.

Functionally equivalent post-consolidation transform with very thorough tests (run, archive metadata, cloud run with and without local execution), but it wires tests.Main and goleak into the whole internal/cmd package and adds proxy-unset hacks to the shared test helper, both unrelated to the task.

Applies the transform correctly after consolidation and has thorough unit, run, archive and cloud-run tests; however it adds a public `lib/executor` API with a CLI-specific error message, an unrelated proxy-unsetting TestMain, and does not handle env or script-layer shortcuts that wipe scenarios before the merge.

Clean executor.ApplyOnce plus a thin CLI wrapper, with the strongest end-to-end tests (archive and cloud-run upload round trips, every conflicting flag, no mutation of the input); it adds an exported lib API, duplicates proxy-env hacks in two TestMains, and misses the cross-layer shortcut edge case.

Structurally closest to the reference: it uses the fork-script rename, errors on a return with a value outside partials, and only lets valued returns escape. But `moveReturnLast` skips forms like `return .Site.GetPage "x"` or `return resources.Get "x"`, which then fail with wrong-arg errors, a regression from the old behaviour. It also changes the input of an existing regression test.

Closest to the reference: a valued return comes back as an error, so a non-partial `{{ return "x" }}` reports the right error. It moves `return f x | g` to `f x | g | return` instead of dropping commands and keeps the fork script in sync. Tests are broad; the main weakness is a duplicated walkTemplate body that also swallows valued returns.

Uses context plumbing plus a new state field to capture partial return values, which is more complex than needed. It edits exec.go without updating the fork script, includes docs edits, silently drops pipeline tails, and ignores returned values outside partials.

The context-pointer approach works for partials and nested templates, but it edits exec.go directly without updating the fork script. It silently drops pipeline commands after return and adds docs churn. The too-many-args test only asserts a confusing Go template error.

Implements `return` as a function that returns a sentinel error, which works anywhere and in any template, and it keeps the fork maintainable by adding a fork-script replacer. However, `return x | f` silently drops the rest of the pipeline, and a return with a value outside partials is silently ignored.

Injects the nested-template recover through the fork script, which keeps the fork maintainable, and the recoverReturn helper is clean. It wraps multi-arg returns but silently drops trailing pipeline commands, ignores valued returns outside partials, and adds an unnecessary applyTransformationsToTree wrapper.

Same core design as C2, including the direct exec.go edits that the fork script would lose, plus docs rewrites the task did not require. `Return` does not validate the argument count, and the `return x | f` silent-drop bug remains.

Takes a C3-like approach with direct upstream exec.go edits (errRecover, walkTemplate) and no fork script update. The Return func has no arg-count check, pipeline commands after return are silently dropped, and docs are edited. Tests are crammed awkwardly into a 404 template.

Handles the whole pipeline after `return` sensibly by wrapping it, and follows the fork-script pattern via `walkTemplateOld`. On the downside, it duplicates the `walkTemplate` body, adds context-based plumbing, relies on the new `errors.AsType`, and adds docs edits.

Early return works in partials, regular templates and nested templates, and `try` re-throws it; `return a | b` is wrapped into one pipe so nothing is silently dropped. However, the return value travels through an extra context-pointer mechanism, the walkTemplate body is copied, valued returns outside partials are silently ignored, and docs edits widen the scope.

The sentinel approach works for early return in partials, pages and nested templates. It edits `errRecover` and `walkTemplate` directly in the forked exec.go without updating the fork script, which is the maintenance burden the issue warned about, and it also silently drops pipeline tails after `return`.

The basic early-return mechanism works, but `return x | f` silently drops the rest of the pipeline. It edits upstream errRecover and walkTemplate in exec.go without updating the fork script, so the changes would be lost on re-fork. Bare-return swallowing depends on TemplateStore.ExecuteWithContext rather than the executor.

Same map-of-slices approach as C2 with a slightly richer table test (mixed for_each and static blocks), but it has the same coarse ConfigResource-level cross-module override that drops distinct child-instance imports.

Keeps every same-module block, which fixes the reported for_each case, but a parent import still drops all child-module imports for that resource, so an instance the parent never targeted is silently lost (fails 2/3 hidden tests); the table-driven plan tests are solid.

Fixes the reported same-module case and returns a flat slice like the reference, but parents still override children per ConfigResource, so a parent import of one instance silently drops child imports for other instances.

Returns an ordered slice like the reference, but parent override still works at ConfigResource level, so a parent import silently suppresses child imports for other instances; good unit and plan tests.

Grouping statements into map-of-slices fixes same-module for_each/count imports, but keeps ConfigResource-level parent/child override, which still silently drops non-overlapping child-module imports; the table tests never cover the cross-module case.
Minimal grouped-map fix for same-module blocks with good for_each, count and module plan tests, but parent-overrides-child is still per resource rather than per instance (fails 2/3 hidden tests).

Fixes the reported case but keeps the coarse cross-module override, and its unit test codifies that bad behavior: a parent import of bar["a"] wipes out the child's bar["b"] import; the slice-aliasing tweak is also unnecessary churn.

Same ConfigResource-level override flaw as C1, and its unit test asserts that a parent import of bar["a"] should discard the child's unrelated bar["b"], locking in the silent drop; the module-path copy is an unrelated change.

Same map-of-slices fix as C2–C4 with decent unit and plan tests (for_each, count, child module), but cross-module dedup stays at ConfigResource granularity, so distinct child-instance imports can still be silently dropped.
Same approach as C1 with an added unit test and a combined plan test; the reported bug is fixed, but child imports for instances the parent did not target are still discarded.

Returns a flat slice and overrides parent/child per instance by statically parsing the instance key, which handles static keys correctly; however, its conservative heuristic for dynamic/for_each targets and its ignoring of module instance keys can still drop child imports, unlike the reference's expansion-time dedup.

Closest to the reference: parent blocks override child blocks only for the same static instance key, but it re-parses the address and treats any dynamic key as an overlap, so parent for_each imports can still drop distinct child imports.
Correctly wraps literals and preserves the positive-duration check with solid tests, but adds an ad-hoc ExperimentalDurationExpr guard in only one rule and does not update DurationExpr.Pretty.

Wraps paren'd literals in a unary-plus DurationExpr in both the paren and unary-offset rules, and extends the positive-duration check to catch (0) and -(5); it does not update Pretty, which can print the unary '+', and the experimental-flag gating only on the unary path is a little inconsistent.

Works in practice, but paren_duration_expr uses an unconditional `$2.(*NumberLiteral)` assertion that would panic on any other node type; it also skips the Pretty fix and adds no error tests for the positive-check logic it changed.

Works and has the most accurate positions (lparen to rparen), but paren_duration_expr does an unchecked $2.(*NumberLiteral) assertion that panics on any unexpected node type; no Pretty fix and no error-path tests.

Wraps bare literals in a unary-plus wrapped DurationExpr in both the paren rule and applyUnaryOpToDurationExpr, fixes Pretty, and keeps the parse-time positive and division/modulo-by-zero checks via durationLiteralValue; it also adjusts the UI serializer so the new `+` node is not printed, though the SUB-wrapping logic in applyUnary is duplicated rather than unified.

Thorough fix: the literal wrapper, a constant-folding positive check, preserved parse-time division/modulo-by-zero errors for (0), a Pretty fix and a matching UI serializer change; the wrapper StartPos excludes the '(' and the UI edits go beyond the reference.

Round-trip is fixed and tests are decent, but durationNumberLiteral only unwraps the wrapped `+` case, so `foo[-(5s)]` loses its parse-time error; Pretty is not updated and StartPos differs between the `+` and `-` paths.
Fixes the round-trip correctly, but the positive-duration helper only unwraps its own Wrapped+ADD node, so foo[-(5)] is no longer rejected at parse time; also no Pretty fix.

Closely mirrors the reference with a single wrapDurationExpr helper applied in both the paren rule and applyUnaryOpToDurationExpr, plus the Pretty fix and a preserved positive-duration check; the UI serializer change is a justified consequence of the new AST shape, and tests span parser, printer, prettier, promqltest and UI.

A single wrapDurationExpr helper is used by both the paren rule and applyUnaryOp, which closely mirrors the reference, plus a positive-duration constant check, the Pretty fix and UI consistency; very complete tests, with the only extra scope being the justified UI edits.

Fixes round-trip by wrapping literals in the grammar actions and keeps the positive-duration parse check, with good printer, error and promqltest coverage, but leaves DurationExpr.Pretty printing a unary `+` and does not centralize the wrap logic in applyUnaryOpToDurationExpr.
Clean wrap of literals in both grammar paths plus a recursive constant check for positive durations; it lacks the Pretty unary-plus fix but has good printer, error and eval tests, including subquery.
